subject: Deal onboarding phases: hardware tethering and cloud-fallback plan
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Allen <jordan.allen@acmeai.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deal onboarding phases: hardware tethering and cloud-fallback plan

Jordan / team —

Following our kickoff yesterday, I wanted to put a single plan on the table for how we’ll tie the Dedicated capacity sizing to Acme’s ramp and vendor lead times. High level ask: confirm which of the three phases below Acme feels comfortable committing to so we can lock OEM reservations and cloud backstop windows.

Phase A — Proof-of-concept (0–2 months)
- Small dedicated pool (8x A100-class equiv) for canary runs and performance tuning
- Use CloudX spot-backed VMs for burst testing (falls back to Dedicated for SLA-critical flows)
- Acceptance: 1 P99 latency target achieved on representative prompt set

Phase B — Initial production (3–6 months)
- Increase to staging pool (32 GPUs) sized from Acme MRP; start reserved OEM pledge for tranche 1
- Split routing: 70% Dedicated, 30% CloudX reserved capacity (to handle burst and onboarding variance)
- Acceptance: stable throughput at 75% of expected peak, autoscale verified

Phase C — Full launch (6+ months)
- Full Dedicated carve (128 GPUs) on-shore; OEM deliveries aligned to monthly tranche schedule
- Cloud backstop reduced to DR-only (10%) after OEM fulfillment complete
- Acceptance: SLA, throttling policy, and rollout playbook approved

Key vendor actions we need from you by EOD next Tue (3 business days):
1) Confirm forecasted monthly inference throughput (tokens/sec or QPS) for months 1–9 (I attached a simple MRP template).
2) Prioritize which regions you require (us-east, us-west) — we’ll use this to align OEM and CloudX inventory holds.
3) Any hard regulatory constraints that force on-prem or VPC-only routing.

Ben, Marissa — once Jordan confirms we should engage CloudX procurement for spot/reserved proration and pull the OEM ETA breakdown. Karthik / Neha — can you confirm fallback pricing for CloudX and whether we can reserve an interim staging pool with their channel partner?

Attachments: acme-mrp-forecast.xlsx (MRP template)

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Allen <jordan.allen@acmeai.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement CloudX <procurement@cloudx.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deal onboarding phases: hardware tethering and cloud-fallback plan

Evelyn — thanks for the clear breakdown. Quick answers below and a few clarifying Qs: 

1) Forecast: I filled the MRP with conservative and aggressive lanes; sending the file back. We expect a phased ramp: 10M tokens/day month 1, scaling to 180M tokens/day by month 9.
2) Regions: us-east priority, us-west secondary.
3) Regulatory: No on-prem requirement initially, but data residency concerns may push some workloads to VPC-only in months 6–9.

Questions for Redwood:
- For Phase B tranches, is it possible to front-load more cloud capacity (reserve seats) if OEM tranche slips past month 4? What are lead-time penalties or pricing impacts?
- For Phase C full carve, do you support a split-delivery (OEM delivers 60% then final 40%) so we can start routing?

I’m looping Li Wei from OEM (cc’d) and Procurement at CloudX so we can get quotes/ETAs straight. I’d like to align on a delivery calendar by next week.

Best,
Jordan Allen
Head of Infrastructure, Acme AI

On Tue, Jul 27, 2027 at 09:12 AM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com> wrote:

> 
> Following our kickoff yesterday...
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Allen <jordan.allen@acmeai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deal onboarding phases: hardware tethering and cloud-fallback plan

Jordan / all —

Short note from Capacity: we can front-load additional CloudX reserved capacity for Phase B but there are two tradeoffs to call out:
1) Pricing: a 3-month short-term reservation via channel will be ~1.6x on-demand for guaranteed hold, vs spot which fluctuates but is cheaper. We should capture the delta in the SOW.
2) Routing complexity: fragmenting traffic (more cloud at start) requires more aggressive prefix caching and KV warmup during rollouts; that increases early engineering effort.

Regarding split deliveries: OEMs are used to staggered shipments. We can accept partial tranche deliveries into our staging pool and start routing as long as we validate KV cache synchronization and model shard mapping. That needs a runbook step to trigger canary rollouts per tranche.

I’m attaching the OEM ETA spreadsheet we requested from Li — it has per-sku lead times and suggested tranche windows. Li, can you confirm these ETAs are locked if Acme signs a non-refundable deposit?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

Attachments: oem-eta-breakdown.csv
From: Li Wei <li.wei@oemcompute.com>
To: Jordan Allen <jordan.allen@acmeai.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deal onboarding phases: hardware tethering and cloud-fallback plan

Hi Jordan / Redwood team —

Thanks for the draft calendar. Confirming OEM stance:
- ETAs in oem-eta-breakdown.csv are conditional on a 30% deposit per tranche. Once deposit received we can guarantee shipment windows within a 2-week variance.
- Split deliveries are supported; we can ship 60/40 but recommend 40/30/30 if you want more frequent incremental validation points.
- Region holds: we can reserve inventory for us-east for up to 90 days with a signed purchase agreement.

I also attached CloudX’s formal reserved-pricing quote. If Acme chooses the short 3-month reserved to bridge OEM lead time, pricing will be as in that quote.

Next steps (suggested):
1) Acme to return signed MRP lanes and indicate preferred tranche cadence by EOD Mon (2 business days).
2) Acme/Redwood to confirm deposit schedule so OEM can lock holds.
3) Redwood to provide a routing/playbook snippet for tranche-based canary rollouts by Friday.

Regards,
Li Wei
Account Director — OEM Sales
OEMCompute

Attachments referenced: cloudx-spot-pricing-quote.pdf
